rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Eviction Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered Los Angeles tenancy without an allowed just-cause reason. For no-fault evictions, the owner may have to pay relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 6 months of tenancy or lease expiration, whichever comes first

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies only after the tenant has lived in the same unit for at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first; excludes specific categories such as transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, an owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, certain nonprofit homeless or substance-abuse treatment facilities, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
coverage.summary: Covers most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including some newer buildings and single-family dwellings.

rules.exemptions: The document lists exceptions including transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, an owner’s roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some nonprofit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.interaction: The JCO covers most Los Angeles residential properties not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance; the page separately notes that AB 1482 may regulate rent amounts for buildings older than 15 years.

rules.effective_date_basis: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.title: Fair Market Rent threshold for nonpayment evictions
rules.requirement: For RSO and JCO rental units in Los Angeles, a landlord may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the amount owed is higher than the applicable Fair Market Rent. The Fair Market Rent depends on the unit’s bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed the applicable Fair Market Rent (FMR)

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to rental units subject to either the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance or the Just Cause Ordinance; the applicable FMR depends on bedroom size.
coverage.summary: Covers all Los Angeles RSO and JCO rental units.

rules.interaction: The document states this nonpayment eviction limit applies to all rental units covered by either the RSO or the JCO.
rules.quoted_span: Applies to all RSO & JCO rental units. Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: AB 1482 statewide annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: For covered California units, annual rent increases are limited to 5% plus the regional change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. For the period August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase stated in the document is 8.9%.

coverage.small_owner_exception: Single-family homes and condominiums are exempt only if not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with at least one corporate member, and the landlord gave the required written notice; the exemption does not apply where there is more than one dwelling unit on the same lot or a second residential unit in the building that cannot be sold separately.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Not covered: units restricted by deed, regulatory restrictions, or other recorded documents limiting affordability to low- or moderate-income households; certain dormitories; units already subject to the City’s RSO.
coverage.summary: Applies to covered California rental units in buildings older than 15 years, with listed exemptions for newer construction, certain affordable units, dormitories, some owner-occupied two-unit properties, qualifying single-family homes and condominiums, and units subject to Los Angeles RSO.

rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years; deed- or regulation-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where the second unit was owner-occupied for the entire tenancy; qualifying single-family homes and condominiums with required notice; units already subject to the City’s RSO.
rules.interaction: The page says the Los Angeles JCO does not regulate rent increases, but state law AB 1482 may regulate rent in buildings older than 15 years, while units already subject to the City’s RSO are listed as not covered under AB 1482.
